newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: NZ SPORT, RUGBY UNION - Osborne back, bigger, heavier and faster.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT, RUGBY UNION - Osborne back, bigger, heavier and faster.

text.p: MELBOURNE, July 25 - Glen Osborne returns to test rugby on Saturday bigger, heavier, stronger, and faster, NZPA reports.
Like last season, North Harbour's Osborne is coming from behind and, like last season, he believes he has just hit top form.
The All Black nicknamed "Oz" will be in no mood to like Australians when his team face the Wallabies in the MCG test under lights.
"We're always in the love-hate relationship," he said of Australia.
"We love to play them and we love to beat them, but we hate to lose to them, no way we want to go down to them in anything."
Promoted to the test side from an expanded reserve squad in place of injured left winger Tana Umaga, Osborne said his callup reminded him of his passage into the All Black team last season.
Then he replaced Jonah Lomu and excelled in all four tests he played in South Africa.
"It's a very similar situation to '96, I came from behind to get into the team," the 26-year-old former Wanganui representative said.
"This time I just have to make sure I don't let Tana or anyone down. I think Tana could have played if he really wanted to. He's a hard and strong guy."

Umaga has been sidelined by an arm and shoulder injury and said he felt there was bruising on his ribs and sternum. He was forced out by the injuries in the All Blacks' 35-32 win over South Africa in Johannesburg last Sunday (NZ time). It was his fifth consecutive test this season.
While the Wellingtonion thrived in the test environment, Osborne waited eagerly on the wings for his chance after recovering from a range of injuries, including a problem ankle.
"I feel in good shape, I think I'm in the form I was in last year in South Africa. I went there without any rugby for about two weeks. Now I've been without rugby for three weeks."
Osborne's inclusion loses nothing in terms of robustness, speed and combination.
He probably adds to the team's cause through his 15-test experience, skills and ability to cover at fullback.
"I regard myself as a winger who can cover fullback, not a fullback who can cover wing," he said.
Under Laurie Mains' regime, Osborne played all of his first 10 tests at fullback in 1995.
He was switched to wing by Hart last season and has ideally gained a couple of kilograms since. His statistics show a marked increase in his strength and speed following a summer training programme.
Hart said he was sorry over the last few weeks for leaving Osborne out of the run-on team because the player was "fizzing, fit and ready after hard work" to play.
"He deserves his place, we haven't lost anything through the replacement," Hart said.
